from.place: Global cup comparison: evaluating the naive/derived diagram on one computing resolution pairing before comparing two resolutions.

title: Homology formula for one realized resolution pairing
statement: Let X be a scheme with its sheaf derived category in universe u. Fix a comparison C from module cohomology to homology of derived global sections [lem-sc-module-cup-derived-class-comparison] and a natural tensor pairing P on derived module homology [lem-sc-module-cup-derived-homology-tensor]. Let μ be a natural family RΓ(A) tensor-derived RΓ(B) → RΓ(A tensor-derived B). For a computing resolution pairing D of F,G [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data], a realizing cochain map t [def-sc-module-cup-realization-complex-data], and a naive section tensor map ν, assume ν has the tensor-section summand formula and that the naive/derived diagram commutes [lem-sc-module-cup-naive-derived-compatibility]. In degrees p,q in the natural numbers, let a,b,c be cocycles in the left, right, and target global resolution complexes, respectively, with c equal to the sectionwise pairing of a,b. Then C carries the target class of c to H^(p+q)(μ followed by RΓ(D.derivedMap t)) applied to P evaluated on the C-images of the two input classes.

source.place: Lemma 20.31.3 and the global cohomology diagram immediately following it

proof.text: Use the on_cycles formulas of C and P to lift all three cycles to integer degrees and form their tensor cycle. The summand formula for ν and Realizes for t identify its image with the output lift after the invertible extension identification. Naturality of homologyFunctorFactors gives the corresponding localized cycle-class identity.

Postcompose the naive/derived diagram with RΓ(Q(t)) and the inverse target augmentation. Naturality of the comparison unit moves Q(t) to the top. Naturality of μ moves inverse input augmentations to the bottom; the explicit derivedMap formula cancels them with the input augmentations. Apply homology and P.natural, then substitute the cycle-class formulas to get the asserted equality.
